director.chapterArc: A tactical collapse into grief and a stranger's arrival.
director.restraintNote: Maintain clinical distance during the death sequences; let the horror land in the silence between actions rather than vocalized shock.

cues.delivery: Garrick's voice is flat and tactical; grief is suppressed under the weight of immediate survival logic.
cues.from: "Gully's thirty yards south. Twenty coming down it. Cart's finished — don't look at the cart, nobody look at the cart, it's finished. Mother can't walk. Marta can't move and hold at the same time." Garrick's blade was out and he did not appear to know it. "So. Wyck. Get on that tailgate and keep the drain side of this cart clear for two minutes. Not three. Two."
cues.through: "Up the gully," Garrick said. "We can't go under them. We're going to go through them, uphill, and here's why: a Husk on a slope can't brace. Tip one at the top and it takes two with it on the way down and does the work for you." He was already moving. "It's the only good news in this entire cut. Come on."

cues.delivery: Toren's internal panic is palpable but contained; the realization of powerlessness must feel physical.
cues.from: "Dad, I can't —" Toren held up his arm, and it was the most useless gesture of his life. The Ember sat dark and shut on his forearm. Under his breastbone there was nothing at all, no warmth, no coin, not even the memory of one. "It's gone. It's all gone, I can't —"

cues.delivery: Garrick's explanation is a lesson in sacrifice; the tone must be weary but absolute.
cues.from: "And then what?" Garrick did not turn around. "A stride is legs, Toren. It is not hands. I'd be standing at the top of that fan with my mother in my arms and nothing in my hands, and Wyck and Milo and Dessa would be at the bottom of it with nothing in theirs, and I'd have to come back down four times through a slope full of those things with no way to cut a single one of them off me." He stepped over a Husk that was still coming apart. "One shape. One job. You pick the job that keeps the most of you standing and then you don't think about the other one again. Not once. Not while it's happening."
cues.through: "That's the whole trade," his father said. "Everybody makes it. Everybody's always made it. Rock."

cues.delivery: Wyck's action is described with staccato precision; the physicality of his stance must feel heavy.
cues.from: Wyck Tanner got up on the tailgate of a broken cart with an iron bar in his hands and held the drain side for two minutes.
cues.through: The second one did the same. So did the third. On the third one he came off the bar and hit it with his fist, which was a mistake, and he split three knuckles open on something inside it that had no business being that hard. He did not seem to notice. He shifted the bar to that hand anyway and kept the drain side clear for two minutes, exactly as asked. When Dessa shouted that Senna was off the cart, he came down off the tailgate backward without ever once turning around.

cues.delivery: Senna's voice is thin but commanding; she projects authority despite her physical state.
cues.from: "Don't fuss," Senna said. Her voice had gone to almost nothing. "Milo. Milo, look at me. Take the front. You're the steadiest."
cues.through: "You are, and I've watched all of you for sixty years, and I'm not going to be argued with on a road." She got her arm across her chest. "Go."

cues.delivery: The description of Marta's power is observational; the narrator must remain detached from the magic.
cues.from: Marta stood twelve feet north of them with her hands out and her palms turned down, and she had not moved her feet in six minutes.

cues.delivery: Marta's final command is delivered with a dry, unyielding warmth; she refuses pity.
cues.from: "Garrick Voss, I have been mending this family since before your son could stand up, and you are not going to stand there and argue geometry with me." Her arms were shaking. Her voice was not. "Milo."

cues.delivery: The ascent is a physical struggle; pacing should mimic the exhaustion of climbing loose shale.
cues.from: Toren went in front with a fist-sized piece of limestone in his right hand because his father had told him to bring a rock and there had not been time to decide whether that was a joke. It was not a joke. It worked about as well as anything works. A Husk went down under Garrick's blade and half rose. Toren put the rock into it. The thing came apart around the rock and left him holding the rock.

cues.delivery: Marta's death must be delivered with absolute stillness; the horror is in what she becomes.
cues.through: Then she was not there anymore, which is a stupid way to put it, and Toren never afterward found a better one. She was a woman who had set his wrist when he was six. She had a braid with gray in it. Her hands lay open on the road. And she was simply, completely, not there.

cues.delivery: Garrick's final moments are described with a slow, heavy cadence; the shortening blade is visual horror.
cues.from: Here is how a man runs out.
cues.through: He got to the edge and Wyck's arms went around him from behind. Wyck weighed a stone and a half more than he did and had a grip like a gate hinge. Toren fought him. It made no difference at all.

cues.delivery: The stranger's arrival is a shift in tone; the narrator must convey Toren's shock without melodrama.
cues.from: That was when the man came off the wall.
cues.through: Then he turned around and went back down to deal with the road.

cues.delivery: The stranger's combat is efficient and alien; the description must feel like a tactical report.
cues.from: There were perhaps twenty-five left in the cut, spread across the whole width of it, and they came at him, because there was nothing else in them to do.
cues.through: Toren watched him and felt something turn over at the bottom of his chest that he did not have a name for yet, and which was not gratitude.

cues.delivery: Toren's realization of the stranger's identity is internal and quiet; a moment of heavy observation.
cues.from: He knelt on the shale with his hand on his father's shoulder and did not say anything, because there was nothing to say and no air to say it with.
cues.through: Toren looked at it for a while without one single thought in his head about it. He was thirteen and his father was dead on the shale in front of him. He noticed it the way you notice the pattern on a plate at a funeral. It went down into him somewhere, and stayed, and did not come back up for a long time.

cues.delivery: The stranger's voice is flat and low; he speaks with the weight of a man who has seen too much.
cues.through: He did not say it to her. He said it to the air in front of him, quietly, with his jaw set, the way a man says a word he has been holding in his mouth for a while and has finally run out of reasons not to spend.

cues.delivery: The healing is clinical and silent; the narrator must not dramatize the supernatural element.
cues.from: "I've met a few." He opened the pack one-handed without looking at it, the way a man opens a drawer in his own kitchen, and took out a roll of cloth and a flat tin. "This is going to be unpleasant and then it's going to be worse and then it's going to stop. Somebody hold her hand. Not the boy."

cues.delivery: The ending is a quiet resignation; the stranger's final action must feel like a heavy burden.
cues.from: "Don't get comfortable." The man took his hands away. He was gray around the mouth. "I've stopped it. I haven't fixed it and I'm not going to be able to. That's a four-week wound on a body that doesn't have four weeks' worth of anything to spend, and if it goes bad we are not going to catch it in time out here."
cues.through: He was trying to think of somewhere else to be.

pauses.after: He did not break. He came down through it. It was a hard, deep, absorbed landing that put him onto one knee with one hand flat on the pavement. The impact banged off both walls. Gray ash jumped a foot into the air in a ring all around him.
pauses.reason: Scene turn: The stranger lands; a moment of shock.

pauses.after: Because that was not a thing. That was not a thing that was. You hold one. You put it down and you pick up the other, and the putting-down takes about as long as the picking-up. His father had told him that thirty-six hours ago, standing by a fire with a tin box in his hands, and had said it the way you say a thing that has been true since before anyone kept a record.
pauses.reason: Revelation: Toren realizes the impossible nature of the combat.

pauses.after: He did not put a hand on Toren's back. He did not crouch. He did not say that he was sorry, or that it had been fast, or any of the other things people say. He stood six feet off with ash on his coat and let it go on for as long as it went on.
